goal: Fix the recurring GitHub Pages Web Serial upload failure and flash the connected ESP32-S3 display from the webpage with the current firmware and font assets.
success_gates: The page no longer loses the selected firmware when the file input handler changes.
The bundled package writes the boot/application image at 0x0 and the FATFS assets image at 0x820000 after a full erase.
Connection cleanup and retry leave the page able to make another attempt without a reload.
A browser Web Serial run reaches erase 100%, write 100%, hard reset, and a visible success state on the connected board.
The device re-enumerates or emits boot evidence after the browser flash.
The deployed GitHub Pages site serves the verified flasher and matching firmware manifest.
An independent review finds no unresolved completion-critical defect.
constraints: Use the webpage for the actual erase and flash; CLI flashing is prohibited.
Preserve the ESP32-S3 partition offset for assets at 0x820000.
Do not change unrelated firmware or site behavior.
Do not claim physical success from build or HTTP checks alone.

effect_policy.device_full_erase_and_flash: authorized by the current user request
effect_policy.repository_push: authorized by the request to fix the GitHub Pages flasher completely
effect_policy.approval_ref: User: use the webpage to upload and flash the program to the screen; do it all on your own.

rollback.site: Restore tracked files from the pre-run Git commit.
rollback.device: Reflash the prior tracked firmware image; erased runtime settings cannot be recovered.

evidence: ESP-IDF merge-bin produced a 1674992-byte image for offset 0x0.
FATFS build produced an 8257536-byte assets image for offset 0x820000.
Five deterministic flasher tests pass, including hashes, offsets, progress, and single ownership of file selection.
Local HTTP checks serve the page, manifest, and complete assets file; esptool-js 0.6.1 CDN responds successfully.
